sop_trash_can_batteries_001.title: Trash Can Not Opening — Battery Fix
sop_trash_can_batteries_001.summary: If the automatic trash can lid won't open, the batteries are likely dead. Replace with 4 AA batteries from the supply closet. If still not opening after replacement, hold the sensor button for 3 seconds to reset.
steps: If the automatic trash can lid is not opening, the batteries are most likely dead.
Remove the lid from the trash can.
Locate the battery pack inside — it will be set to Lock. Switch it to Unlock and open it.
You need 4 AA batteries. Go to the supply closet and find the battery shelf on the 3rd shelf from the bottom, all the way to the right.
Grab a plastic pack of 4 AA batteries.
Open the pack and insert all 4 batteries following the diagram inside the battery pack.
Close the battery pack, lock it back up, and put the lid back on the trash can.
Wave your hand over the sensor to test it.
If it is still not opening after the battery replacement: hold down the small sensor icon on the right side for 3 seconds. This resets it. Then wave your hand again — it should open normally.
Note: this reset is usually needed because a kid held the sensor down too long and accidentally locked it out.

sop_group_membership_001.title: Creating a Group Training Membership — Protocol
sop_group_membership_001.summary: How to set up a CrossFit group class membership in Wodify. Used for members completing on-ramp, experienced CrossFitters joining from another gym, or any combination.
steps: This membership is used when: a member has completed their on-ramp, someone is joining from another CrossFit gym with existing experience, or any combination of those situations. Everyone ends up needing a group training membership.
Go to app.wodify.com and log in with your admin username and password.
Go to People, then Athletes.
Type in the member's name and open their account.
Tap Add Membership.
Select the membership tier they agreed to — Unlimited, 3x per week, 2x per week, etc.
Set the start date to match what they need. This date becomes their billing date going forward unless a hold is placed, in which case the billing date will shift.

Walk through the membership agreement with them: they agree to auto-renew, they agree to 30 days notice for cancellations, and they agree to 30 days notice for holds. Make sure they understand each of these before initialing.
Have them initial each section and sign the agreement.
Check if payment is already on file. If not, have them enter their payment info — credit and debit cards only, no bank accounts accepted.
Once everything is signed and payment is confirmed, they are good to go.
If they have not used the Wodify app before, walk them through how to use it before they leave.
Send them off with a great day!

sop_remote_signup_001.title: Remote Sign-Up — When Member Is Not In Person
sop_remote_signup_001.summary: How to sign someone up remotely when they are not in person. Create their membership in Wodify (agreements send automatically), send the waiver, then send the copy-paste text below to walk them through their 3 emails.
steps: Create their membership in Wodify — make the Personal Training membership first. The agreement will be sent to them automatically via email.
Also send over the gym waiver separately.

Send them the following text message:

Hey FIRST NAME, here are the next things you should see in your inbox — there are 3 emails.

The first email is your agreement. Go ahead and look everything over, sign it, and upload your payment information there.

The second is a waiver to sign. Please sign the waiver before your first workout with us — it is just agreeing to standard Texas liability and release for a gym.

The third email is your welcome to Vegvisir email. In that email you will find your welcome packet and be able to download the Wodify app.

When you get a chance, let me know when you would like your first personal training session and we will get that scheduled. Other than that, let me know if you have any questions. Welcome to the Vegvisir family — we cannot wait to train with you!
Check back in about an hour to see if everything has been completed.

If they have not completed everything by the time of their first session: alert the coach they are meeting and let them know the member still needs to sign their agreements. The member can sign everything when they come in.
Respond to any questions they have as they fill things out. Be straightforward and honest. If you are unsure about something, ask a manager.

sop_sales_avatars_001.title: The 5 Sales Avatars — Who Walks Through Our Door
sop_sales_avatars_001.summary: The 5 most common prospect types at Vegvisir, what they need to know, their usual objections, and how to overcome them.
steps: AVATAR 1 — Financially Conscious but Highly Motivated: This person has researched us heavily — seen the website, Instagram, maybe an ad. They are excited but budget-constrained (grad student, just changed jobs, living with parents, etc.). They need to know exactly how we can help them specifically. Learn their goals and anchor all value to those goals. Recommend more PT than they expect. Their objection will be price. Response: 'Could you afford the regular monthly rate? Great — in this first month we are asking for a little more investment. In our experience this takes people from staying 7 months to 31+ months. At a bare minimum we need 4 PT sessions — how does our $499 one PT / two CrossFit class package sound?' Once you give the price, go quiet. Whoever speaks first usually loses. If they still object, bring it back to their stated goals: 'You said you want to lose weight and you are really motivated. I would hate for us to stop because of an extra $200. Let's invest upfront and get you the results you want — and if you do not see them, come talk to me and I will make it right.'

AVATAR 2 — The Person Who Knows What They Want: They know they want PT and group classes. They just need to know we can help them. Attach your pitch to past success stories of similar people. Their usual objection: they want to skip straight to group classes but have not done CrossFit. Remind them this journey can be dangerous without on-ramp. Say: 'We have helped over 1,000 people and learned that without on-ramp, the journey does not stick. Even if you end up hating this gym, you will leave knowing how to do a clean and snatch safely. We have had experienced athletes go through on-ramp and gain a ton from it.'

AVATAR 3 — The Social Butterfly: They want group classes to meet people. They still need on-ramp. Say: 'You will meet your coach and people in due time — but it is hard to connect with others when you are worried about not knowing movements or getting hurt. The hybrid option lets you learn effectively so that when you are in group class, you can actually enjoy it. Your coach will also learn about you and tell other coaches how to help you, making it even easier to connect.'

AVATAR 4 — The Lifelong CrossFitter: They want to go straight into classes. Their objection is that we are more expensive than other gyms. Response: 'We want our coaches to have a real career in this. Most CrossFit gyms have not raised prices in over 10 years. Our rates reflect our downtown rent and our commitment to coach quality. You will get more value here than you have anywhere else — and our prices are firm. We stand behind that.'

AVATAR 5 — Just Moved and Looking for a Gym Nearby: This is the coldest lead and the hardest to sell. They do not know us at all. Tell them everything — what we do, that we are a coaching gym, ask them about their problems and attach what we do to each one. At the end when price comes up, ask what range they were looking for and get as close as you can. Say: 'If you are looking for under $100 we cannot help. But if you are looking for coaching and you want this problem fixed, it is a lot cheaper than going it alone and quitting again. We have held so many people accountable to hitting their goals.'

PRACTICE TIP: Think of all the questions someone might ask, then set up a test No Sweat Intro with another coach. One of you plays the prospect, one plays the coach. Switch and repeat. This is the best way to get comfortable with all 5 avatars.

sop_adaptive_athletes_001.title: Coaching Adaptive Athletes — Protocol
sop_adaptive_athletes_001.summary: How to coach athletes with prosthetics, limited mobility, or other adaptations. Focus on empathy, problem-solving, and communicating solutions to the rest of the coaching team.
steps: When working with an adaptive athlete (prosthetics, wheelchair, limited sensation, etc.), start by identifying exactly what their adaptation is and what equipment or prosthetics they use.

Put yourself in their position. Think about what life would be like with that adaptation. Example: below-the-knee amputation with a prosthetic foot — what would squatting feel like with a hard piece of plastic where your ankle should be? Use this empathy to proactively think through movement limitations before they come up.
Apply those adaptations to the movement. Example: if they cannot move their ankle, treat it like a fixed ankle and make the appropriate scaling adjustments.
Offer your solution and ask: 'Does that help?' If yes, ask if there is anything else you can do. If no, ask: 'Okay, help me understand what the issue is so we can make a plan together.'
When problem-solving, always give 3 solutions and 1 recommendation. Let them choose the solution that suits them best.

Once a solution is agreed on, say: 'Let's implement this. I will let the other coaches know. In your next workout we will see if this works — if not, we will try one of the other solutions. Is there anything else I can help with today?'
After the session, communicate the chosen solution to all coaches so everyone is prepared the next time that athlete comes in.

sop_returning_dropin_001.title: Returning Drop-In — Protocol
sop_returning_dropin_001.summary: How to handle a drop-in who has visited before. Look them up in Wodify, offer to charge their card on file, and make them feel remembered and welcome.
steps: Go to app.wodify.com. Go to People, then Athletes.
At the top you will see a filter for active memberships — click All, then type in the person's name.
Open their account and check if they have a credit card on file.

If they have a card on file: offer to add the drop-in to their account and auto-charge the card. If they prefer, they can also go through the standard drop-in procedure — send them the class link for their requested time.
Make them feel remembered and welcomed. Say something like: 'Hey [Name], great to see you again! How has everything been? We cannot wait to train with you — here is the link for the [time] class!'

sop_instagram_follow_001.title: Someone Follows Us on Instagram — Protocol
sop_instagram_follow_001.summary: When someone follows Vegvisir on Instagram, follow them back and send a welcoming DM. Guide them toward a free intro or drop-in based on their response.
steps: Follow them back on Instagram.

Send them the following message: 'Hey [First Name]! We are so happy you followed us! Are there any fitness questions we can help you with? If so, let us know — we are happy to help as soon as possible!'
Respond to their reply following our values — be helpful, honest, and curious.
If they seem interested in joining, guide them toward booking a Free Intro.
If they are looking to drop in, help them through the drop-in process (refer to the Drop-In Booking Protocol SOP).

sop_membership_change_down_001.title: Membership Change — Downgrade for Next Month
sop_membership_change_down_001.summary: How to temporarily lower a member's membership tier for the next month and revert it back the following month. Membership tiers: 4x/mo $113, 8x/mo $215, 12x/mo $225, Unlimited $239.
steps: Membership tiers available: 4x/mo = $113, 8x/mo = $215, 12x/mo = $225, Unlimited = $239.
Go to app.wodify.com. Go to People, then Athletes. Search and open the member's account.
Click their current membership. Hit Generate Next Membership.
Once the next membership generates, change the number of attendances to match the lower tier they are moving to.
Go to their invoice and change the invoice amount to the appropriate dollar amount for that lower tier.
Then generate the membership for the month after that and change it back to their original membership tier so it reverts automatically.
They do not need to sign anything. Let them know what you did and how many times they can come in during the upcoming month.
Note: if they are downgrading and have drop-ins, they can apply drop-in fees as credit up to half the value of their membership — this is currently only valid on the $215 (8x/mo) membership.

sop_membership_change_up_001.title: Membership Change — Upgrade for Next Month or Immediately
sop_membership_change_up_001.summary: How to upgrade a member's CrossFit membership for the next billing cycle or partway through the current month using a custom invoice for the difference.
steps: Go to app.wodify.com. Go to People, then Athletes. Search and open the member's account.
Open their current membership and set it to deactivate at the next renewal date.
Create the new upgraded membership starting on that same renewal date.
Let the member know the agreement has been emailed to them and that they need to sign it before the renewal date.
IF THEY WANT TO UPGRADE BEFORE THEIR NEXT RENEWAL DATE (mid-month): go to their account and tap New Invoice.
Set the invoice to auto-charge today. Create a custom invoice — title it 'Membership Increase Adjustment'.
Set the dollar amount to the difference between their current membership and the new one.
Hit Save. The invoice will run and the upgrade takes effect immediately.

sop_change_forwarding_number_001.title: Changing the Gym Phone Forwarding Number
sop_change_forwarding_number_001.summary: How to change which phone number receives forwarded calls from the gym line. Must be confirmed with owner Kidd before making changes.
steps: IMPORTANT: Confirm with the gym owner Kidd before making any changes to the forwarding number.
Go to app.gymleadmachine.com and sign in using the admin profile: kidd@vegvisircrossfit.com.
Enter the password and the one-time password provided.
Once logged in, go to Settings, then Profile.
Go to Call Settings.
Find the Forwarding Number field and update it to the correct phone number.
Hit Save.

sop_failed_payment_001.title: Failed Payment — Protocol
sop_failed_payment_001.summary: How to handle a failed membership payment. Priority is making the member feel respected while resolving the balance. Grace period of 5 days for emergencies like stolen cards.
steps: Priority 1: make the member feel welcome and not ashamed. Priority 2: resolve the balance — we cannot render services without payment.
Go to app.wodify.com. Go to People, then Athletes. Search and open the member's account.
Find the open invoice on their account. Tap the invoice number.
Go to Actions, then tap Pay Invoice, then select Default Card. Note the response.

IF THE RESPONSE IS 'does not allow this type of purchase' OR 'card deactivated': reach out to the member with friendly language: 'Hey [First Name], we tried to run your balance but ran into a small issue. Things like this totally happen — can you go ahead and check the invoice in your email and update your card information? If you have any trouble, let me know and I can help you do it through the Wodify app.'

IF THE RESPONSE IS 'insufficient funds': do not reach out yet. Let the system retry up to 3 times. If it still does not go through after 3 attempts, then reach out: 'Hey [First Name], there is an invoice due at the gym and we have been having some trouble running your card. Let me know if you need help updating it through the Wodify app.'
For any card issue: give a grace period of up to 5 days before stopping services. If it is a genuine emergency like a stolen card, be flexible and communicate with the owner.
In all communications use friendly, non-confrontational language. The member should never feel attacked — just informed.

sop_extended_dropin_001.title: Extended Drop-In (Visiting for a Month) — Protocol
sop_extended_dropin_001.summary: For drop-ins staying for an extended period, verify their CrossFit experience (6+ months required), then set them up with a regular group membership with no auto-renew.
steps: First confirm they have 6 or more months of CrossFit experience at a real CrossFit gym. We do not allow anyone without this experience to drop in — even for an extended stay.
Ask for their home CrossFit gym and verify it is a legitimate gym (refer to the Drop-In Eligibility SOP).
Take their info from Gym Lead Machine and create a new athlete profile in Wodify.
Once the athlete profile is created, go to New Membership and select the appropriate tier — Unlimited, 12x/mo, or 8x/mo based on what they need.
Set the start date to the day they begin.
If using Quick Add: after saving, open the membership, go to Actions, and hit Stop Auto-Renew. If using Customize: turn off auto-renew before saving.
Email them to let them know they have a waiver to sign, an agreement to sign, and a welcome email with the Wodify app download.
Let them know the membership will end one month after their start date and will not auto-renew.

sop_custom_prorated_membership_001.title: Custom Prorated Membership — Protocol
sop_custom_prorated_membership_001.summary: For members (90+ days) who need a custom number of classes due to a date change, extended stay, or other situation. Prorate based on their membership tier.
steps: This is only for members who have been with us for 90 days or longer.
Ask the member how many classes they need before going on hold or canceling.
Go to app.wodify.com. Go to People, then Athletes. Open their account.
Generate a new membership starting on the date of their first class.
Use their usual membership tier as the base. Treat Unlimited as 15 classes, 12x as 12 classes, and 8x as 8 classes.
Select Customize for their membership type. Change the number of attendances to the number of classes they need.
Calculate the prorated price: (classes needed / total classes in tier) x membership price. Example: 6 classes out of 12 = 6/12 x $225 = $112.50.
Set the price to that prorated amount and hit Save.
Let the member know the membership has been created and that they just need to sign the agreement. Once signed, they can start booking into classes.

sop_door_not_closing_001.title: Front Door Not Closing — Fix
sop_door_not_closing_001.summary: If the front door is not closing properly, use an Allen wrench to adjust the door closer arm at the top left of the door. Counterclockwise = slower, clockwise = faster.
steps: The door is likely not closing because it is bouncing off the middle plate or closing too slowly, causing the latch to miss.
Go to the supply closet and grab an Allen wrench from the tool drawer — the mesh bucket on the 3rd shelf of the chrome shelving unit. You may need to grab the full set to find the right size.
Go to the door closer — the small box at the top left of the door with the arm attached.
On the left side of that box you will see two Allen wrench holes — one on top and one on the bottom. You want the one on TOP.
If the door is closing too fast and bouncing: turn the Allen wrench counterclockwise (to the left) to slow it down.
If the door is closing too slow and not latching: turn the Allen wrench clockwise (to the right) to speed it up.
Adjust until the door closes all the way on its own without bouncing, and the magnetic lock catches cleanly.
Return the Allen wrench to the tool basket in the supply closet.

sop_sales_sheet_001.title: Using the Sales Sheet — Protocol
sop_sales_sheet_001.summary: How to use the 2025-2026 Sales Sheet in Google Sheets to track leads, consultation bookings, show rates, and front-end revenue.
steps: The Sales Sheet is in Google Sheets and is titled '2025-2026 Sales Sheet'. If you do not have access, request it from management.
When a new lead comes in through the website, a pricing form, or a referral from a current athlete, add their name to the sheet.
Under Notes, write how you know them or what the next step is.
Your goal is to get every lead on the list booked for a consultation. Call them once per day for up to 3 days in a row until they book or go cold.
Once they book, mark Yes in the Booked column.
After their consultation: if they showed up mark Yes. If they did not show, mark No Show and note the reason if known.
If they signed up: enter the front-end revenue from the sale in the Sold column.
If they did not sign up: note the reason in the Sold column (e.g. price, not ready, etc.).
Notes should always contain the most current next step for that lead.
At the end of each month, all data is collected and reviewed. A new month starts fresh.

sop_family_emergency_001.title: Member Has a Family Emergency — Protocol
sop_family_emergency_001.summary: When a member reaches out about a family emergency, lead with care and compassion first. Membership decisions are secondary. Follow the Emergency Hold SOP if needed.
steps: Lead with care — making the member feel supported is the priority. Membership logistics come second.

If it is a bereavement (someone has passed): 'We are so sorry to hear this. We hope that you and your family find the healing you need right now. Please do not worry about anything here — we are thinking of you.'
If someone is in the hospital: 'We are so sorry to hear this. We hope they heal quickly. Please let us know if there is anything we can do to help during this time.'
If they are personally hurt or dealing with something difficult: ask how they are doing and what, if anything, we can do to help.
If they ask for a membership hold: follow the Emergency Hold SOP.
If they need to leave and are unsure when they will return: run it by the General Manager or Owner (Kidd) before offering an emergency cancellation. Kidd will approve or not based on the situation.
In all communications, ask questions that make the member feel genuinely cared for. Make it clear we are doing everything we can to help them — not just manage a membership.

sop_member_thinking_of_leaving_001.title: Member Thinking of Leaving — Protocol
sop_member_thinking_of_leaving_001.summary: When a member says they are thinking of leaving due to a bad experience, escalate the communication channel as high as possible and use the 1 problem, 3 solutions, 1 recommendation framework.
steps: When a member says they are thinking of leaving due to a bad experience, respond immediately with empathy: 'We are so sorry to hear that — that is never what we expect for any of our athletes. Would you be available for an in-person check-in at your earliest convenience? We would love to sit down, talk, and see what we can do to make this right.'
If in-person is not possible, offer a phone call. If not that, a video call. Get the conversation as high up the communication ladder as possible — avoid handling this over text or email if you can.
If text or email is the only option, keep it tactful. Ask questions, listen, and avoid being defensive.
Your goal in the conversation is to understand the root of the problem. Ask questions until you know exactly what went wrong.
Apply the framework: 1 problem, 3 solutions, 1 recommendation. Your recommendation should involve both you and the member working together toward what they originally came here to achieve.
Refer to the Membership Exchange SOP if the solution involves swapping their remaining membership value for PT or drop-ins.

sop_book_checkin_001.title: How to Book a Check-In Appointment
sop_book_checkin_001.summary: Check-ins do not have their own membership type. Book them as a Free Intro in Wodify so both coach and athlete can sign in without a membership error.
steps: Confirm the date and time with the person you are doing the check-in with.
Go to Appointments, then Calendar, then New Appointment.
Enter the correct date, time, your name, and the athlete's name.
For the appointment type, select Free Intro.
Hit Save.
This allows you to sign both yourself and the athlete in without the system flagging a missing membership.

sop_2on1_criteria_001.title: Who Qualifies for a Free 2-on-1 PT Session
sop_2on1_criteria_001.summary: The 4 criteria a member must meet before being offered a free 2-on-1 personal training session for a friend.
steps: The member must meet all 4 of the following criteria before you offer a free 2-on-1 PT session:
CRITERIA 1: You and at least one other coach genuinely enjoy working with this person every time they come in. They make your day better.
CRITERIA 2: They clearly align with our values — Humble, Hungry, and Human Smart. There is no friction with this person.
CRITERIA 3: They have mentioned that they have a friend who is interested in Vegvisir.
CRITERIA 4: They have been a member for 90 or more days.

If all 4 criteria are met: offer the free 2-on-1 PT session and let the owner (Kidd) or the current General Manager know for approval. If you have been coaching here for over a year, approval is implied — but if you start offering this 2-3 times in a single month and people are not signing up, expect a conversation with ownership.
If they sign up each time, this is a great thing and is actively encouraged.

sop_kansa_study_001.title: Kansa Study Sign-Up — Protocol
sop_kansa_study_001.summary: When a new participant signs up through the Kansa Study, reach out to book a call, conduct a mini NSI, onboard them as a new athlete, and follow the hybrid membership SOP.
steps: You will receive an email from the Kansa Study saying 'New Participant' with their contact info.

Reach out using the preferred form of communication and say: 'Hey [First Name]! We are so excited to have you be a part of the Vegvisir CrossFit family! Can you give us a time that would be best for a call so we can tell you more about what to expect and set up your first appointment?'
Work with them to find a time that works for both of you.
On the call, conduct a mini No Sweat Intro: learn their goals, learn how we can help them, and make a plan.
Let them know they will be doing 4 to 8 personal training sessions before transitioning into group classes. Start with 4 and adjust from there based on their progress.
Make sure they leave the call with a clear plan.
Post a New Athlete Alert in the #new-athletes Slack channel. Include their first and last name, any adaptations, their goals, and how we can help them over the next 14 weeks.
Create their membership following the Hybrid / On-Ramp Membership SOP — treat it as a 4x PT / 4x CrossFit (8x total) on-ramp membership.

sop_charge_invoice_001.title: How to Charge or Create an Invoice
sop_charge_invoice_001.summary: How to charge an existing invoice or create a new custom invoice in Wodify.
steps: TO CHARGE AN EXISTING INVOICE: go to app.wodify.com. Go to Financial, then Invoices. Click the invoice you need. Go to Actions, then Charge Invoice. Select the default payment method on file.
TO CREATE A NEW INVOICE: go to the athlete's profile. Tap + Invoice or New Invoice. Select the purchase type — choose from the existing options or create a custom invoice for something else.
For a custom invoice: name the invoice clearly (e.g. 'Membership Increase Adjustment'), set the correct price, set it to Auto Pay, and confirm the amount matches what was agreed upon.
Hit Save. The invoice will auto-charge at 12:01 AM.
If you need to charge it immediately: go to Actions, then Pay Invoice, and select the default payment method.

sop_ku_research_journey_001.title: KU Research Client Journey SOP
sop_ku_research_journey_001.summary: Step-by-step process for onboarding, training, and offboarding athletes enrolled in the KU Research Study. Covers intake call, PT sessions, class transition, exit testing, and membership conversion.
steps: STEP 1 — Initial Contact: Upon receipt of an email from KU, email the participant (PPT) asking for a good day and time to call.

STEP 2 — Intake Call: On the call, learn why they wanted to start the study, their current limitations, and what a 10/10 experience would look like for them over the next 14 weeks. Convey all of this info to the team via Slack upon completion of the call. Once done, create their membership and confirm their first Personal Training date.

PT SESSION STRUCTURE: Athletes will receive 4-8 personal training sessions depending on their needs before entering group classes. Sessions can be performed as 2:1 or 3:1 at the 10 AM time slots Monday, Wednesday, and Friday — but other times are acceptable if needed.
IF MORE THAN 8 PT SESSIONS ARE NEEDED: confirm with Kidd before the 8th session to review roadblocks and constraints preventing group classes from being the right path forward for that athlete.

STEP 3 — Team Updates: After the 1st and 4th personal training sessions, update the team via Slack with the athlete's necessary adaptations and current trajectory. Also share the date and time of their first group class.
FIRST PT SESSION REQUIREMENT: The 1st personal training session MUST begin with the B1 and B2 tests.
IMPORTANT — RPE: ALL athlete scores must have RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) recorded at every session without exception.

STEP 4 — Group Classes: The athlete continues into regular group classes and can return to personal training any time they like. The Member Engagement Coordinator (MEC) will keep track of their progress. All coaches must record RPE for each workout along with the usual data recorded during class.
STEP 5 — Exit Testing (Week 13): Upon completion of the 13th week, the MEC contacts the athlete to schedule their exit workout. The B1 and B2 tests are performed again to measure progress.

STEP 6 — Membership Conversion: Upon completion of the program, offer the athlete their current membership to continue at Vegvisir. Discuss avenues to relieve the financial burden such as FSA/HSA accounts, and if they were referred by TIRR, discuss options with TIRR directly.

sop_first_90_days_001.title: Client Journey — First 90 Days
sop_first_90_days_001.summary: The full athlete journey from sign-up through 90 days. Covers onboarding, Slack updates, check-ins, membership renewal, and long-term engagement milestones.
steps: SIGN-UP: When an athlete joins, the person who sold the membership lets the Member Engagement Coordinator (MEC) know. The athlete's info is entered into the On-Ramp page, a brief is posted in #new-athletes on Slack (which auto-populates the Athlete Check-In Sheet), and any personal connections, hobbies, or work info are uploaded to the Affinity Sheet.

WELCOME VIDEO: Once those 3 sheets are updated, the MEC sends the new athlete a video message saying: 'Hi, my name is [First Name]. Welcome to the Vegvisir family! We cannot wait to see you at your first workout. Please text me any time to let me know how we can help you best or if you have any questions — I am here to help as soon as possible. Welcome to the family and we cannot wait to see you!' Mark it as sent on the On-Ramp page.

AFTER 1ST SESSION: The coach who ran the session posts in #current-athletes on Slack with any adaptations the athlete needs or anything the team can do to improve their experience beyond normal class corrections.

END OF FIRST MONTH: At the last personal training session of the first month's membership, the coach must perform a check-in and invite the athlete to sign up for their next membership. If they sign up, post in #current-athletes letting the team know they have moved on and how to best support them. If they do not renew, notify Kidd (owner) immediately and follow the appropriate follow-up procedures.

ONGOING — MEC WEEKLY TEXTS: The MEC texts the athlete weekly throughout their journey. Key milestones to remind them of: 30-day check-in, 60-day check-in, and 90-day check-in. Upload all check-in notes to #current-athletes with the athlete's name so the app can update.

90-DAY CHECK-IN: The MEC conducts the final close-range check-in and lets the athlete know that after this point check-ins will shift to every 90 days. They will still hear from the MEC about their 100th class, 250th class, upcoming events, and other engagement touchpoints to keep them connected to the gym.

sop_ku_workout_upload_001.title: KU Adaptive On-Ramp — Uploading Workouts & Recording RPE
sop_ku_workout_upload_001.summary: For KU Research Study athletes, every personal training workout must be uploaded into Wodify and RPE must be recorded in the comments. This is required by the study.
steps: Go to app.wodify.com. Scroll to the bottom and tap the Extensions tab.
Select Kiosk Plus and open the Coach Board.
Select the least busy class of the day — usually the 9 AM class. Tap that class.
Search the athlete's name and tap Sign In.
Tap the 3 dots underneath their profile picture that appears.
Select Put In Custom One.
Make sure Non-Benchmark is selected.
Type in the workout exactly as it was performed.
Hit Save.
In the Comments field, type: RPE [number on a scale of 1-10].
This step is mandatory for every KU Research Study session without exception.

sop_pt_client_handover_001.title: Handing Over a Personal Training Client — Protocol
sop_pt_client_handover_001.summary: When a PT client needs to transfer to a new coach, the transition takes a full month and is done gradually so the athlete never feels abandoned. Treat it like introducing a trusted friend, not a handoff.
steps: Treat this transition seriously. PT clients form tight relationships with their coaches. A hasty handover is one of the most common reasons we lose personal training clients. Approach this like helping them find someone they will trust just as much.

FIRST HALF OF THE MONTH (weeks 1-2): The outgoing coach runs all workouts and leads all sessions as normal. The incoming coach attends every session, observes, builds rapport with the athlete, and learns exactly how things are done for this client.

SECOND HALF OF THE MONTH (weeks 3-4): The incoming coach writes and executes all workouts. The outgoing coach attends every session in a shadow role — not leading, just present — making sure that everything the athlete has come to know and love is being honored by the new coach.
END OF THE MONTH: Ask the athlete directly if they are comfortable with the transition.
If YES: complete the coach transition. The new coach takes over fully.

If NO: bring in Kidd for a follow-up call to find the right solution. This may mean keeping the current arrangement longer, finding a different coach, or having a candid conversation about what the athlete needs. If the outgoing coach has a path issue, talk with Kidd about adjustments that work for both the coach's career and the athlete's experience.

sop_sandbag_cleaning_001.title: Sandbag Area — Cleaning Protocol
sop_sandbag_cleaning_001.summary: If there is dog hair or dirt around the sandbags, blow it out first with the leaf blower, then scrub with the green automatic scrubber, then blow again. Plug in and return all equipment when done.
steps: Get the leaf blower from the back of the supply closet — it is hanging from the hooks at the back. Insert a charged battery.
Open the garage door.
Blow out all dog hair and dirt around the sandbag area, directing debris out through the garage door.
Close the garage door.
If hair or dirt remains, get the green automatic scrubber. The power button blends into the handle so look carefully for it — it is a different color from the rest of the handle.
Bring the scrubber to the sandbag area and scrub to remove remaining dog hair and debris.
Blow the area again with the leaf blower and direct everything out through the garage door.
Plug in the batteries used on both the leaf blower and the scrubber.
Return both pieces of equipment to where you got them.

sop_impromptu_checkin_001.title: Impromptu Check-In — Protocol
sop_impromptu_checkin_001.summary: When an athlete declines a formal check-in, conduct an impromptu version through casual conversation. Still log it in #current-athletes and ask for a Google review if they are thriving.
steps: If an athlete does not want to do a formal check-in, you can still conduct one informally. You can still log it as a check-in in #current-athletes.
Ask casually: 'Hey, you do not have to do a check-in — but how are you doing? How is your journey going? Are you happy?'
Listen carefully to their response.

If things are going well: congratulate them genuinely. Then ask: 'Is there anything we can do to help you even more?' If nothing, move on. If something, help them in the best way you can following the gym's values.
If things are not going well: help them problem-solve. Ask: 'Is there anything we can help you with?' Help them feel cared for and follow up with the team.
Close with: 'All right, cool — thank you. That is really all I needed to know.'
If they are having a great time: ask if they would be willing to leave a 5-star Google review and hand them the QR code.
If they are struggling: let the team know in #current-athletes how you are going to help them and what the plan is.
Log the check-in notes in #current-athletes with the athlete's name.

sop_frayed_bands_001.title: Frayed or Damaged Resistance Bands — Protocol
sop_frayed_bands_001.summary: If a band has a nick you can see through or a deep fray across the whole band, it is done. Cut it, trash it, and notify the owner when stock of any color drops below 8.
steps: Inspect bands regularly. A band is done if: you can see through a nick to the other side, or there is a very deep fray running across the full width of the band.
If a band meets either of those criteria: bring it to the front desk.
Grab scissors and cut the band so it is completely inoperable.
Throw it in the trash.
If the count of any color band drops below 8, notify the gym owner (Kidd) so the supply can be replenished.

sop_lead_nurture_overview_001.title: Lead Nurture — Overarching Process
sop_lead_nurture_overview_001.summary: The high-level lead nurture flow from first contact through 3 call attempts. Call within 5 minutes of receiving a lead. Text if no answer. After 3 attempts, mark on the sales sheet and let automation take over.
steps: Whenever we receive a lead's contact info — through a website form, CrossFit form, or personal training form — call them within the first 5 minutes. Calling within 5 minutes makes us 98% more likely to sign them up compared to letting it linger.

If they do not pick up: send a text saying — 'Hey [Name], this is Coach [Name] from Vegvisir CrossFit, just calling to see if I can answer any questions for you. Would love to chat and see how I can help!'
If they do not respond: call again the next day at the same time. Call again the day after that at the same time.
After 3 unanswered call attempts: go to the Sales Sheet, mark 'Called 3x', and let the automatic text sequences follow up from there.
If at any point they pick up and give you a callback time or book an appointment: follow up on that exactly as promised. Stay true to your word.
For more detail on the first call script, pricing conversations, and booking the NSI, refer to the First Call Script SOP.

sop_first_call_script_001.title: First Call Script — Turning a Lead Into an NSI Booking
sop_first_call_script_001.summary: How to conduct the first call with a new lead. Goal is always to get them in person for a No Sweat Intro. Deflect pricing questions and anchor value to an in-person visit.
steps: When they pick up, say: 'Hi, is this [Name]?' Wait for confirmation. Then: 'Hi [Name], this is Coach [Your Name] from Vegvisir CrossFit! I saw that you filled out a form on our website and I wanted to see if I could help answer any questions you had.'

Answer their questions with the goal of getting them in person for a No Sweat Intro. In-person visits convert far better because the athlete gets a feel for the gym, the coaching, and the culture — and they have fewer chances to talk themselves out of it.

IF THEY ASK FOR PRICING: do not give a full breakdown. Say: 'Typically our CrossFit members spend around $225 a month, with the first month being a bit more. Personal training sessions typically run around $85 per session. But honestly, it really depends on your needs — we build everything a la carte when you come in, talk through your goals, and make a real plan. We have helped over 1,000 people do this. When would be a good time for you to come in?'

Once they agree to come in and a date and time are confirmed, say: 'Awesome — we cannot wait to see you on [date/time]. You will get a confirmation text from me and a confirmation email. Is there anything else I can help you with today?' If no, say: 'Perfect — have a wonderful day and we will see you on [date]!' Then hang up.
Go to their account in Gym Lead Machine. Go to Appointments, then New Appointment. Enter the confirmed date and time with the coach available at that time.
Send them the NSI Confirmation Text (refer to the NSI Confirmation Text SOP).

IF THEY DO NOT WANT TO COME IN YET: say — 'Totally understand! Is there a better time for me to follow up after you have had a chance to think about it?' Get a specific date and call them back on that date.
IF THEY ARE NO LONGER INTERESTED ON FOLLOW-UP: say — 'No problem at all — we are grateful for your time. If anything changes, we would love to see you in the future.' End the call warmly.

sop_gate_latch_stuck_001.title: Gate Latch Stuck — Fix
sop_gate_latch_stuck_001.summary: If the gate latch is extended and stuck beyond the gate frame (door closed too fast), use a credit card or the gate code plus firm pressure to retract the latch and close the gate.
steps: This happens when the gate closed too quickly and the latch extended past the plate, getting wedged between the plate at the top of the gate and the frame itself.
OPTION 1 — Credit Card Method: slide a credit card or flat card against the latch at an angle and push the latch inward until it retracts enough to close the gate.

OPTION 2 — Gate Code Method: enter the gate code on the other side of the gate. Twist the knob hard while slowly pushing the gate forward just slightly — enough to create a little give. Do NOT push so hard that the top plate breaks. As you keep twisting, the latch should retract on its own and the gate should close normally.

sop_parking_block_post_001.title: Parking Block Metal Post Sticking Up — Fix
sop_parking_block_post_001.summary: If a metal post from a concrete parking block is poking out, hammer it flush with the block. Be careful not to crack the concrete.
steps: Go to the supply closet and find the hammer in the tool drawer — the mesh bucket on the 3rd shelf of the chrome shelving unit.
Walk outside to the parking block with the protruding metal post.
Hammer the metal post down until it is flush with the surface of the concrete block.
Be careful not to strike the concrete itself — only hit the metal post. Stop as soon as it is flush.
Return the hammer to the tool drawer.

sop_bring_a_friend_followup_001.title: Bring a Friend — Post-Event Follow-Up Text
sop_bring_a_friend_followup_001.summary: After a friend attends a Bring a Friend event, send a follow-up text to gauge their experience and guide them toward a consultation or future event.
steps: After the event, send the friend the following text: 'Hey FIRST NAME! This is Coach COACH NAME from Vegvisir CrossFit. How was your workout with us today?'
IF THEY RESPOND POSITIVELY: reply with — 'I am glad to hear it! Would you like to hear more about joining the Vegvisir family, or will we catch you at the next Vegvisir family event?'
IF THEY WANT TO LEARN MORE ABOUT JOINING: set up a consultation time and treat them as a regular lead from that point forward (refer to the First Call Script SOP and NSI SOP).
IF THEY RESPOND NEGATIVELY AT ANY POINT: respond with empathy following our gym values. Try to help problem-solve in the best way you can. Let Kidd know of any issues so they can be addressed.

sop_hsa_fsa_001.title: HSA/FSA — How to Help an Athlete Use It
sop_hsa_fsa_001.summary: Athletes can use HSA or FSA to cover up to 30% of their membership cost through Truemed. Send them the qualification link and help them understand their two payment options.
steps: If an athlete asks how to use their HSA or FSA, send them this link: https://app.truemed.com/crossfit/qualify/tm_qual_qlqzxf3ea5
Tell them: 'Go ahead and fill out the survey at that link — Truemed will take care of the rest for you!'
IF THEY ASK ABOUT HOW PAYMENT WORKS, explain there are 2 options depending on how their HSA/FSA account is set up:
OPTION 1 — HSA/FSA Card: they pay directly with their HSA or FSA card and Truemed handles the tax documentation on the back end.
OPTION 2 — Regular Payment + Reimbursement: they pay normally and Truemed reimburses them approximately 30% afterward.
Let them know they will need to confirm which method applies to their specific HSA or FSA account — this part has to be handled on their end, but the Truemed link is how they get the 30% applied.
If they have further questions about their specific plan, encourage them to contact their HSA/FSA provider directly.

sop_remote_programming_principles_001.title: Remote Programming — Core Principles
sop_remote_programming_principles_001.summary: The overarching principles for writing remote programming for any client. If these are followed, clients stay. If any one of them fails, that is usually why a remote client leaves.
steps: CORE PRINCIPLE: Every remote workout must do three things — (1) you can explain to the athlete how it helps their specific goals, (2) you can explain the intention of the workout and how it gets them closer to their goals that day, and (3) it actually does get them closer to their goals. If all three are true, the athlete will feel confident every time they open their programming because they trust it will make them better. They will stay motivated and see results over time. If any one of these three fails, that is typically why a remote client leaves.

VARIETY: You can follow the same weekly structure and repeat similar movements cycle to cycle, but add variety each week by adjusting reps, weights, or workout format. Clients do get bored, so small changes go a long way. The structure can stay the same — the details should evolve.

PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD: The default progression system is 6 to 12 reps. Start movements at 6 reps and increase by 1 rep each week as the athlete completes everything as written. Once they reach 12 reps, increase the weight, drop back to 6 reps, and begin the cycle again. This typically runs in 8-week cycles before movements are refreshed.

WEEKLY DEADLINE: All remote programming must be completed and uploaded to TrueCoach before Monday at 4 PM. Athletes typically begin their week after that point. Earlier is always better — ideally the week before.
VIDEO LINKS: Every movement in a remote program should have a video attached so the athlete always knows exactly how to perform it correctly.

NOTES AND ADJUSTMENTS: Use the notes field in TrueCoach to give context — if an athlete reported soreness, offer a scaling option. If they hit a milestone, acknowledge it. If something is new, explain why it is being introduced. These small touches are what separate good remote programming from great remote programming.

sop_remote_programming_home_gym_001.title: Remote Programming — Home Gym Client (Brendan-Type)
sop_remote_programming_home_gym_001.summary: How to program for a busy professional training at home with limited equipment. Focus on mobility, tennis or sport performance, and progressive strength with 10 minutes of high-intensity cardio at the end. All programming must work within available equipment.
steps: CLIENT PROFILE — Brendan Type: Busy professional (4 workouts per week), sport-specific goals (tennis), mobility limitations (thoracic spine tightness, limited ankle flexion from prior Achilles injury), limited home equipment. Goals: feel better, play tennis longer, reduce injury risk.

WEEKLY STRUCTURE: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday = strength + metcon days. Wednesday = 30-minute easy bike (nasal breathing focus) + mobility work. Saturday = reminder to play tennis. Sunday = recovery/mobility workout.

EQUIPMENT TO PROGRAM AROUND: Echo bike, low pull-up bar (usable for rows), adjustable incline bench, dumbbells 5-35 lbs, 25 lb kettlebell, resistance bands (10-40 lbs circular), 16-inch box, mobility wedge for ankle flexion, foam rollers. Note: Bowflex dumbbells up to 45 lbs are available but unreliable for explosive movements — keep Metcon weights at 35 lbs or below for safety.

STRENGTH STRUCTURE: 3 movements x 3 sets each. Focus on single-leg balance work (for tennis), calf strength, knee stability, chest and shoulder strength. Use the 6-to-12 rep progressive overload system. Attach a video to every movement.

METCON STRUCTURE: 10 minutes of high-intensity cardio at the end of the session. Use AMRAP or EMOM formats. Build around available equipment — bike calories, dumbbell incline bench press, etc. Keep it short and intense. Example: For Time — 15 cal bike / 15 DB incline bench press at 20 lbs, 10 cal / 10 DB bench, 5 cal / 5 DB bench.

MOBILITY DAYS: 30-minute easy air bike (nasal breathing). Change mobility drills slightly each week to keep it fresh — alternate between standing and quadruped hip CARs, focus primarily on thoracic spine and hip mobility, include ankle flexion work using the wedge.

WEEKLY COPY PROCESS IN TRUECOACH: Check the boxes at the top of each TrueCoach workout block, hit Command+C (Mac) or Ctrl+C (PC) to copy, then paste to the following week. Review whether the athlete completed everything as written. If yes, increase reps by 1. If they have reached 12 reps on a movement, increase weight and drop back to 6 reps.

NOTES: Use the notes field to give conditional guidance. Example: 'If you felt soreness last week, drop to 20 lbs and hold 2 seconds at the top. If you felt good, go for 9 reps at 25 lbs.' Check what they actually did and adjust accordingly the following week.

NEW CYCLES (every 8 weeks): Keep the warm-up and core movement patterns the same but introduce new movements or variations. Write new Metcons each cycle. Start within the athlete's comfort zone and build to beyond it by week 8.

sop_remote_programming_high_level_001.title: Remote Programming — High-Level Athlete at the Gym (Max-Type)
sop_remote_programming_high_level_001.summary: How to program for a high-level, high-volume athlete who trains at the gym and follows the class programming with added accessory work. Expect flexibility in what they actually complete and don't take it personally.
steps: CLIENT PROFILE — Max Type: High-level athlete with significant injury history (meniscus, labrum, mid-back tightness, knee cave tendency on squats). Wants games-athlete-level volume but inconsistent follow-through. Will send videos, request mid-week changes, and skip workouts without warning. Do not take this personally — program robustly and adjust as needed.

PROGRAMMING APPROACH: The first strength portion and the Metcon always follow what the gym class is doing that day. Pull up the gym's programming in Coach View and use it as the base. Add accessory work that feeds into the same muscle group or skill theme as the day's class.

ACCESSORY LOGIC: If the class is pressing and pulling, program push/pull accessory or shoulder stability. If the Metcon is leg-heavy, add leg accessory. If the class is snatches, add explosive work like box jumps. If the class is gymnastics, add high-skill gymnastics like handstand walking or muscle-up progressions. If the class is cleans, add explosive accessory. The theme of the day drives the accessory.

STRENGTH PROGRESSIONS: Use progressive overload week over week. Current working maxes to reference — back squat ~225 lbs, clean and jerk ~285 lbs, deadlift ~420 lbs. Increase weight incrementally each week. Do not cap it until he hits a true heavy for the day.

INJURY NOTES: Watch for knee cave on all squats — add notes and cues every time. He prefers lighter squats but wants heavier squats — you have advised him correctly and he does not always listen. Program correctly and note it.
MOBILITY AND WARM-UP: Focus the optional warm-up on mid-back, hips, and ankles. These are his biggest limiters.
FLEXIBILITY: He will pick and choose from what you write. Write a full week anyway. If he requests a mid-week change, make it — this is part of working with this type of athlete.
PARTNER WORKOUTS: He typically does a partner workout on Saturday mornings at 8 AM. Include this in the programming and note it so he knows what to expect.

sop_remote_programming_busy_member_001.title: Remote Programming — Busy Member Training at the Gym (Danielle-Type)
sop_remote_programming_busy_member_001.summary: How to program for a member who is too busy for regular classes but trains at the gym on their own schedule. May include family members on the same program with individual scaling. Alternates strength focus every two weeks.
steps: CLIENT PROFILE — Danielle Type: Too busy for regular classes but comes in on their own time. May have family members (e.g. kids) on the same program who do her programming with individual scaling. All train together and follow the same structure with initials marking individual adjustments.

WEEKLY ALTERNATING STRUCTURE: Week A = back squats + deadlifts. Week B = strict press + front squats. These four movements are the biggest bang-for-your-buck lifts for building general strength quickly. Alternate every two weeks.

STRENGTH PROGRESSION: Add weight or add reps each week — not both. If you add weight, drop by 2-3 reps. If you add a rep, keep the weight the same. Use a heavy set of 5 as the target. Each family member gets their own weight noted with their initials.

METCON STRUCTURE: Alternate between AMRAP and EMOM formats week to week to add variety. Use compound movements that burn calories efficiently. When programming AMRAPs, estimate how long one round takes for this athlete, add a small buffer (e.g. 3:10 estimate becomes 3:30 goal), and set the time cap to give them a realistic target. Hitting their round goal more often than not is good for motivation.

FAMILY MEMBER SCALING: Each person gets individual weights and modifications noted inline with their initials. Example: Danielle = 95 lbs, Zoe = 35 lbs, Alex = 85 lbs or band row substitute if knee is bothering him. Always include a video for any substitution movement.

MOBILITY: Include an optional mobility section at the end of each session. Rotate between movements like Jefferson Curl, seated forward fold, supine figure-four stretch, and 90/90 hip stretch. Keep the same general structure but rotate movements to prevent burnout.

COPY PROCESS IN TRUECOACH: Go back 2 weeks in TrueCoach (not last week — alternate weeks remember), copy that week, paste it to the current week, then adjust strength weights and reps, write a new Metcon, and update any scaling notes for each family member.

INJURY ADJUSTMENTS: Always check in on any ongoing injuries before finalizing the week. If a member cannot do a movement, substitute something that targets the same muscle group without aggravating the injury. Note the substitution clearly with a video.
DEADLINE: All programming must be uploaded to TrueCoach before Monday at 4 PM.

sop_safe_to_leave_onramp_001.title: Safe to Leave On-Ramp — Criteria
sop_safe_to_leave_onramp_001.summary: The 5 criteria an athlete must meet before they are considered ready to leave on-ramp and join regular group classes.
steps: CRITERIA 1 — Self-Awareness: The athlete knows what they can and cannot do. They understand their own limitations and are not attempting movements beyond their current ability without guidance.

CRITERIA 2 — Knows Their Scales: The athlete has a general idea of their scaling options across all three movement categories — Gymnastics, Weightlifting, and Cardio. They do not need to have every scale memorized cold, but they should have a working understanding of what adjustments apply to them.

CRITERIA 3 — Can Take Instruction: The athlete is coachable. They are able to make changes to their form based on visual cues (watching a demo), verbal cues (being told what to fix), or tactile cues (being physically guided). If a coach gives a correction, it lands.

CRITERIA 4 — Knows the Flow of Class: The athlete understands how a class runs and can be ready to perform when timers are called. They are not consistently behind, confused about transitions, or needing extra time to understand what is happening next.

CRITERIA 5 — Equipment Setup: If the athlete requires special equipment (e.g. a box, a specific bar, bands, a wedge), they can either set it up themselves or a coach can help them set it up in under 90 seconds.

sop_coaching_checklist_l1_001.title: Level 1 Coaching Checklist
sop_coaching_checklist_l1_001.summary: The foundational checklist every coach must complete every class. Master Level 1 before advancing to Level 2.
steps: Show up 15 minutes prior to class.
Welcome each athlete by name as they walk in the door. Ask how they are feeling.
Class starts on time.
Warm-up is briefed by couplet or triplet — NOT the whole thing at once.
Movements are shown correctly before starting the warm-up.
Every athlete is given at least one cue or checked in on during the warm-up.
Strength portion movements are demonstrated correctly before athletes begin.
Athletes are asked if they want to know their numbers.
All athletes are moving safely during strength — correct anyone who is not.
Numbers are recorded on each athlete's profile after their last lift.
MetCon brief is read aloud and all scales are described.
All athlete questions are answered before the MetCon starts.
All athletes are moving safely during the MetCon — correct anyone who is not.
Scores are recorded for each athlete after the MetCon is done. Record exact scales used.
Post-WOD stretch is demoed.
A timer is set for each portion of the workout following the workout plan and times.
Class ends on time.
Athletes are told: 'See you next time, NAME.'
Bright Spot Friday is done during the last 3 minutes of class on Fridays.
No phone use throughout class.
All equipment used in class is returned to its proper spot.
Coach is wearing a shirt that says Vegvisir CrossFit or CrossFit — no other gym's CrossFit gear.
Upcoming events are gone over every class.
Athletes are given their numbers as soon as the brief is finished.
Athletes are told: 'See you tomorrow, NAME.'

sop_coaching_checklist_l2_001.title: Level 2 Coaching Checklist
sop_coaching_checklist_l2_001.summary: Level 2 builds on Level 1 with purposeful cueing, focused points of performance, and higher-quality athlete interactions. Must complete all of Level 1 first.
steps: All of Level 1.
At least one movement in the warm-up brief is given a purpose that connects to the upcoming strength and/or MetCon.
All cues are 14 words or less.
At least one point of performance is highlighted during the brief, demonstrated correctly, and explained in terms of how it will help athletes in the future.
Cues are given to each athlete during the strength portion.
At least one point of performance is given for the MetCon on one movement — explained in terms of how it will help athletes during the MetCon and in future goals.
All athlete questions are answered in 14 words or less.
All athletes are cued at least once during the MetCon to improve virtuosity of movement.
Post-WOD stretch starts with at least 3 minutes left in class.
Any PRs in class are written up on the PR Board.
Fist bump every athlete after the MetCon.
Coach gives at least one compliment to each athlete during class.
Athletes are told to clean up their stuff at the end of class — hold them accountable. No one leaves without cleaning up.
Birthdays are congratulated at the beginning of class.

sop_coaching_checklist_l3_001.title: Level 3 Coaching Checklist
sop_coaching_checklist_l3_001.summary: Level 3 introduces goal-based coaching, tighter cues, and deeper athlete connection. Must complete all of Level 1 and 2 first.
steps: All of Level 1 and Level 2.
All athletes are asked how they are feeling AND what their goal for today's class is.
At least one movement in EACH warm-up couplet/triplet is given a purpose connecting it to the strength and/or MetCon.
All cues are 9 words or less.
Coach gives cues to each athlete during the warm-up.
All athletes are given an intention to chase during the strength portion that relates to their goal for the day.
All cues given during strength are reassessed on each athlete to confirm the cue worked and has been maintained.
Coach gives at least one compliment to each athlete during the strength portion.
Coach sets a countdown timer or gives a verbal countdown for how long athletes have to put away their bars and equipment.
Each athlete is given an intention for the MetCon based on their goal for the day.
At least one SPECIFIC compliment is given to each athlete. ('I love how you are...' counts. 'You're doing great' does not.)
Motivation Monday is held during the stretch: 'What are we all wanting to accomplish this week? It could be anything from buy a banana to climb Mount Everest!'
All athletes receive one compliment on their way out the door.
Individual athletes are invited to upcoming events in a personal way. Example: 'Hey, you have a dog — why don't you sign up for our monthly dog walk group!'

sop_coaching_checklist_l4_001.title: Level 4 Coaching Checklist
sop_coaching_checklist_l4_001.summary: Level 4 raises the standard with full visual coverage, pre-class preparation, and tighter cues. Must complete all of Level 1, 2, and 3 first.
steps: All of Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3.
Coach sees every athlete during every set of the warm-up.
Every movement in the warm-up is given meaning that connects to the workout later in class.
All cues are 5 words or less.
Boards with athlete numbers for the strength portion are written before class and handed out to athletes at the end of the warm-up and before the strength brief.
Rowers and/or bikes are pulled out for the total number of people in class before class starts.
Coach gives a cue AND a compliment to each athlete during the warm-up.
Coach gives at least 2 compliments to each athlete during the strength portion.
At least two athletes at the end of class are told about a future workout in the week that will help them with something that was worked on during class.
No athlete phone use throughout class.

sop_coaching_checklist_l5_001.title: Level 5 Coaching Checklist
sop_coaching_checklist_l5_001.summary: Level 5 is the highest standard of coaching at Vegvisir. Every athlete is coached as an individual with full connection to their journey and goals. Must complete all of Level 1, 2, 3, and 4 first.
steps: All of Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, and Level 4.
Each athlete is addressed during the warm-up by connecting movements to their overall journey and goals. Example: 'We are doing this because we have been working on X to improve Y.'
Visual, tactile, and short verbal cues (5 words or less) are all used throughout the day. At least one of each type is used in the warm-up, strength, and MetCon.
Coach asks each athlete about how a Work, Family, Hobby, or Friend thing is going — showing genuine personal interest.
Coach helps athletes clean up their weights and makes sure everything ends up in the proper spots.
Athletes are asked to take out and put up the correct number of rowers, bikes, and boxes for the next class.
Texts are sent after class to athletes who did not show up — reach out to get them to schedule their next classes.

sop_no_coaching_while_training_001.title: Can I Work Out In a Class I'm Coaching?
sop_no_coaching_while_training_001.summary: No. When we coach, we coach. When we train, we train. These are two separate roles and cannot be done simultaneously.
steps: No — you cannot work out in a class you are coaching.
When we coach, we coach. When we train, we train. These are two entirely separate responsibilities.
Even with just one athlete, your responsibility is to provide the best possible coaching experience for them. You cannot coach well with your heart rate at 150 bpm.
If you want to train, do it outside of your coaching hours.

sop_coaching_main_class_programming_001.title: Programming Main Class Workouts
sop_coaching_main_class_programming_001.summary: The full system for programming main class workouts at Vegvisir. Covers new cycle setup, week-to-week programming, Metcon selection, progressive overload, testing week, and monthly coach prep.
steps: SETUP: Keep two tabs open at all times — app.wodify.com (where programming is entered) and coach-dashboard-api.onrender.com (the WOD Search tab, used to look up historical workouts, filter by time domain, and pull past notes/RPE). There are two modes: New Cycle Start and Continuous Programming. Cycles run 8 weeks.

NEW CYCLE — STEP 1: Review the last cycle before deciding anything. Check Slack for how check-ins have been trending. Check Gym Lead Machine for member messages that should influence programming. Walk the floor and coach classes to note common faults you are seeing live.

NEW CYCLE — STEP 2: Pick exactly 3 goals for the cycle — one from each bucket: 1 weightlifting focus (e.g. hip mobility in bottom of squat), 1 gymnastics focus (e.g. pulling strength toward muscle-up), 1 cardiovascular focus (e.g. short time-domain output).

NEW CYCLE — STEP 3: Select core lifts that build toward those 3 goals. Every cycle must always include: back squat, a pulling barbell movement (deadlift, clean pull, etc.), an Olympic lift, and a pressing movement. Bench press must appear at least every other cycle — skipping it two cycles in a row causes member pushback.

NEW CYCLE — STEP 4: Decide on a 6-, 7-, or 8-day rotating structure. 6-day = each lift moves backward one day per week. 7-day = lifts migrate around the week so regulars don't feel stuck doing the same Monday workout every week. 8-day = each lift moves forward one day per week.
NEW CYCLE — STEP 5: Program Week 1 in full, then copy it forward week to week in Wodify and adjust numbers for progressive overload.

PROGRESSIVE OVERLOAD (Strength): Start by establishing a rep max (e.g. 10-rep max back squat on Week 1). Then run 3 sets at ~70% of that max, increasing ~2% per week (72%, 74%...) until approaching theoretical max (~78%). Then drop to a lower rep scheme and repeat the climb. By the final testing week, be testing the exact quality built toward in Week 1.
CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 1: Bulk copy the previous week's full set of days forward onto the current week's dates in Wodify.

CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 2: Open each day and update the strength portion. Warm-up structure stays consistent for the lift of the day — only the Metcon-specific warm-up portion changes week to week. Update the working percentage per the overload plan. Keep coaching notes and comments — these should be dialed in during Week 1.

CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 3 (Metcon Selection): Every 3-day span must satisfy two independent rotations simultaneously. TIME DOMAIN: one Long (17+ min), one Medium (10-17 min), one Short (under 10 min). INTENSITY: one High (thrusters, burpee box jump-overs, squat cleans — fast and heart-rate-spiking), one Medium, one Skill/Light. These two rotations run in parallel — a workout's time domain and intensity are separate calls. Also avoid stacking same-movement-pattern days back to back. Use WOD Search to browse options filtered by the day's strength movement.

CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 4: Pull the chosen workout into Wodify. In WOD Search, filter history to find prior occurrences and copy notes forward — but verify they are still accurate. Confirm or set RPE. Set formatting to the standard template: time-domain header bolded, movements with prescribed loads, scaled options beneath. Set the time cap or goal rounds/reps. For EMOMs: coach scores if there are built-in rest periods; athlete scores if there are no rest periods. Add a post-WOD stretch targeting whatever muscle group the workout stressed most.
CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 5: Progressively overload the accessory work the same way as the main lift, unless it is pure stretching or mobility — that can stay static for the whole cycle.
CONTINUOUS PROGRAMMING — STEP 6: Add a short targeted warm-up piece that primes whatever the Metcon calls for. Keep total warm-up length under ~15 minutes.

TESTING WEEK AND CYCLE TRANSITION: The final week's tests should mirror exactly what Week 1 set out to build. Plan the next cycle before you get here — aim to always be thinking ~8 weeks ahead. Send member-facing communications: new cycle announcement, testing week hype content, explanation of how the programming serves the membership's goals, and direct response to any concerns members have raised.

MONTHLY COACHES MEETING (1st Saturday of every month): Come prepared ~4 weeks ahead with a list of any new or different movements appearing in warm-ups that month so coaches are never caught off guard mid-class.

STANDARD FOR DONE WELL: Before finalizing each week, ask yourself — would you personally be excited to walk in and do this programming? Would the gym's top 5 most engaged members be excited? If the honest answer is no, revise before publishing.

sop_coaching_head_programmer_role_task_0.title: Role & Task List — Head Programmer (Main Class Workouts)
sop_coaching_head_programmer_role_task_0.summary: Accountability checklist for the head programmer role. Covers weekly, per-cycle, and monthly non-negotiables plus the judgment standards that separate effective programming from just filling in workouts.
steps: WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Reviewed Slack check-ins for the week — noting whether results and feedback are trending favorable or flagging something to work on.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Reviewed Gym Lead Machine for any member messages relevant to programming decisions.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Spent time on the floor coaching and observing classes — not just building workouts from a desk.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Every day programmed follows the 3-day balance rules (time domain mix, load mix, movement-pattern spacing, intensity spacing) — not just filling in a workout.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Strength progression numbers updated correctly per the cycle's overload plan — not copy-pasted without adjustment.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Historical notes and RPE checked and confirmed still accurate before reusing — not blindly copied forward.
WEEKLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Warm-ups stay under ~15 minutes and are primed for that day's Metcon and strength focus.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES (every 8 weeks): 3 cycle goals chosen — 1 weightlifting, 1 gymnastics, 1 cardio — explicitly tied to member feedback and observed faults, not chosen arbitrarily.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Cycle constants present — back squat, a pulling barbell movement, an Olympic lift, a pressing movement.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Bench press included if it was skipped last cycle.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Rotation structure (6/7/8-day) chosen deliberately.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Testing week built to mirror Week 1's tested qualities.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Next cycle already planned and drafted before current cycle's testing week arrives.
PER-CYCLE NON-NEGOTIABLES: Cycle-transition member communications sent — new cycle announcement, testing week hype, programming explanation content, response to any open member concerns.
MONTHLY NON-NEGOTIABLES: Coaches meeting prep completed by the 1st Saturday of the month — list of new or different movements coming up in the next month's warm-ups shared with coaches ahead of time.
JUDGMENT STANDARD — Planning horizon: thinks ~8 weeks ahead at all times. If programming feels reactive or last-minute, the role is not being run at standard.
JUDGMENT STANDARD — Willing to change course mid-plan: if a workout choice is not landing right, able to catch it and pivot rather than force the original plan through.
JUDGMENT STANDARD — Preserves institutional knowledge: does not rewrite notes and RPE from scratch each time a workout repeats. Pulls and verifies historical data so quality is consistent over time.
JUDGMENT STANDARD — Treats this as a retention tool, not a task to clear: programming is core to how members get results while having fun. It should be treated with weight.

JUDGMENT STANDARD — Self-check before publishing: would you be excited to do this week's programming yourself? Would the gym's top 5 most engaged members be excited? If the honest answer is no, it is not done.

JUDGMENT STANDARD — Comfortable driving change management: new movements, cycle transitions, and shifts in focus create friction for coaches and members if introduced without warning. This role owns getting ahead of that friction through coaches meeting prep and member communications.

sop_late_athletes_001.title: Handling Late Athletes — Protocol
sop_late_athletes_001.summary: Warm-up runs on a fixed schedule regardless of late arrivals. Athletes who show up late catch the next couplet or triplet. Very late athletes get a late warm-up sheet from the front desk. Warm-up always ends on time.
steps: The warm-up runs on a fixed schedule. Each couplet or triplet of warm-up movements is done every 5 minutes regardless of who has arrived. Example for a 5 PM class: at 5:05 you are on the 2nd couplet or triplet, at 5:10 you are on the 3rd.
If an athlete shows up a few minutes late: they simply catch up on the next couplet or triplet. No special accommodation needed — athletes should expect this.

If an athlete shows up 7-10 minutes late: grab one of the late warm-up sheets from the front desk. Hand it to them and say: 'Hey, I am sorry you showed up late — do this and it will get you warmed up. If you have any questions let me know, but these should be movements you already know.'
Watch the late athlete as you would anyone else in class and help them get caught up with the same amount of attention you would give any other athlete during the warm-up.
The warm-up always ends on time. It does not stretch to accommodate late arrivals — ever.

sop_athlete_injury_decision_tree_001.title: Athlete Says Something Hurts — Decision Tree
sop_athlete_injury_decision_tree_001.summary: How to handle an athlete reporting pain or injury. We cannot diagnose or prescribe — but we can adapt, facilitate, and bridge gaps. Covers acute vs. chronic, loss of power, tightness, and activation issues.
steps: LEGAL BOUNDARY: We cannot diagnose injuries or prescribe a plan to fix them. We CAN execute plans given to us by licensed practitioners (PCPs, PTs, doctors) and we can adapt movement to work around limitations. Our knowledge bridges a lot of gaps — but stay in our lane.
STEP 1 — Is the injury ACUTE or PERSISTENT? Acute = something suddenly hurts when they move, and it hurts a lot. Persistent = it is just kind of always there.

ACUTE INJURY — STEP 2: Is there loss of power? Example: they try to press a dumbbell and suddenly cannot, or they try to sit down and cannot use that knee. If YES — this is a real injury requiring a medical professional. Tell them to see a doctor as soon as possible. If they choose to stay, adapt around that body part and do not let them work through it. If NO (just tightness when moving) — continue to the next step.

ACUTE INJURY (no loss of power, just tightness): Help them work around the tightness. Think about the body as a series of levers — muscles pull, they do not push. If their knee hurts and their knees are caving in during a squat, think about what connects to the knee and what is causing the cave. Do NOT have them lift heavy, jump, or do anything that loads that area. Instead, make a positional adjustment. Example: turn toes out and raise heels slightly to relieve a tight hip and allow a deeper, safer squat. This is within our scope.

PERSISTENT INJURY — STEP 2: Is it getting worse with movement or staying the same? If GETTING WORSE — adapt around it, do not let them use that body part in your care, and strongly recommend they see a doctor especially if it has lasted 2 or more weeks. If STAYING THE SAME (just an ongoing annoyance like an achy shoulder) — move to the next step.

PERSISTENT INJURY (not getting worse): This is usually a chronic movement fault — they have been moving incorrectly over a long period of time and it is building up. Identify how they are moving incorrectly. Example: knee soreness after workouts = too much pressure on the knee = likely knee cave during squats. This is an ACTIVATION issue. Do not have them add weight. Instead, give them a drill to feel the correct muscles firing. At the bottom of the squat, cue them to drive their knees out. Help them feel what it means to activate the right muscles. If they cannot feel it, give them drills until they can.

SUMMARY — Acute sharp pain with loss of power = send to a doctor. Acute tightness without loss of power = positional adaptation, no heavy loading. Persistent and getting worse = adapt around it and send to a doctor. Persistent but stable = activation work and movement correction.
